assessment: This manuscript by Chang et al. reports the evolutionary patterns of Y-chromosome evolution in Drosophila, providing perhaps the most comprehensive interspecific comparison of Y chromosomes available to date. They focus on four species of the melanogaster species subgroup and do extensive sequencing and assembly. The manuscript describes the pattern of divergence in these chromosomes, and uses comparative approaches to compare the drivers of evolution in flies and mammals. The authors suggest that the Y chromosome uses a different mechanism to repair double strand breaks than on autosomes. We were impressed by the novelty and rigor of the work as well as the overall presentation of the results.
